materials.name: Iron
materials.notes: Standard wrought iron. Tier 1. SRD baseline. Common across smiths.

materials.name: Steel
materials.notes: Carbon-iron alloy. Tier 1-2 split depending on quality. Used in weapons and tools.

materials.name: Bronze
materials.notes: Copper-tin alloy. Older than iron; ritually preferred in some traditions for not 'arguing with the moon.'

materials.name: Copper
materials.notes: Soft, conductive. Tinkering reagent; alchemical conductor.

materials.name: Tin
materials.notes: Soft, low-melt. Pewter precursor; alloy component for bronze and bell-metal.

materials.name: Lead
materials.notes: Heavy, dull, toxic over long handling. Used to line caskets, write curse tablets, line scrying basins (blocks divination).

materials.name: Silver
materials.notes: Tier 2. Common silvering surcharge on weapons against undead/lycanthropic creatures (SRD baseline).

materials.name: Gold
materials.notes: Tier 3 by value. Soft for weapons; used in inlay, ritual implements, coin substrate.

materials.name: Electrum
materials.notes: Gold-silver alloy. Tier 2-3. Coin metal in some regions; ritually 'between worlds' for psychopomp work.

materials.name: Cold Iron

witness_payload.witness_summary: Forged below freezing without flame quench; resists fey, abjurations, and Imposed bindings.

materials.notes: Tier 2. Folkloric (Celtic, Slavic) anti-fey iron. In this world: forged cold, never touched by flame after pour. Reduces effectiveness of charm/binding effects by 1 step when used as substrate.

materials.name: Meteoric Iron

witness_payload.witness_summary: Star-fall metal. Holds memory of its descent: any item forged of it dreams of falling. Witness binding rolls inherit memory_tag 'starfall'.

materials.notes: Tier 3. Classical (Iliad references meteoric iron weapons). Rare; usually arrives as ore in craters or already-worked relics. Mythology: 'fell from where the sky is thin.'

materials.name: Orichalcum

witness_payload.witness_summary: Pre-civilizational copper-gold alloy attested in old hymns and ruined temple inscriptions. Resists tarnish; rings when struck even across rooms.

materials.notes: Tier 4. Lifted in pattern from Plato/classical Atlantis lore. Functionally: a metal that should not still exist; sometimes pulled from ruins. Strikes with a bell-clear tone. Cannot be forged with mundane fire; requires a Composed condition (canon-cost).

materials.name: Granite
materials.notes: Common igneous building stone. Tier 1.

materials.name: Limestone
materials.notes: Soft, common. Base for lime-mortar; carves easily; weathers.

materials.name: Slate
materials.notes: Fissile. Roofing, writing tablets, Bell Court ledger boards.

materials.name: Marble
materials.notes: Tier 1-2. Civic and religious construction; takes polish; veining matters to carvers.

materials.name: Obsidian
materials.notes: Volcanic glass. Sharpest natural edge; brittle. Ritual knives, scrying mirrors. SRD- and Mesoamerican-attested.

materials.name: Jade
materials.notes: Tier 3. Funerary and protective in many traditions. Tough — survives drops that shatter softer stones.

materials.name: Chalk
materials.notes: Soft, friable. Marks circles, doors, names. Cheap and everywhere.

materials.name: Soulstone

witness_payload.witness_summary: Crystalline matrix capable of holding a fragment of cognition. Used in necromantic and animistic crafts to anchor an echo of a person, animal, or pact.

materials.notes: Tier 3-4. Pattern lifted from D&D 5e soul gems + animistic stone traditions; renamed for honesty. Risk: improper handling can bind a fragment of the holder. Cleric/heretical-surgery contraband in many cities.

materials.name: Oak
materials.notes: Hardwood. Standard structural and weapon-haft wood. Tier 1.

materials.name: Ash
materials.notes: Flexible, shock-absorbent. Tool handles, spear shafts, bows.

materials.name: Pine
materials.notes: Softwood. Cheap, plentiful, resinous. Building, crating, kindling.

materials.name: Yew
materials.notes: Longbow wood; poisonous heartwood. Folk-belief: grows in graveyards because it likes the company.

materials.name: Blackthorn
materials.notes: Dense, dark, wickedly thorned. Cudgels, walking staves. Folklore (Celtic): cuts both physical and curse-thread.

materials.name: Ironwood
materials.notes: Tier 2. Hardwood dense enough to dull blades; sinks in water. SRD-attested; carved only with cold-chiseling or sorcery.

materials.name: Darkwood
materials.notes: Tier 3. SRD: rare hardwood half the weight of normal wood at twice the strength. Used in shields and bows where weight matters.

materials.name: Ghostwood

witness_payload.witness_summary: Wood cut from trees that grew on or through a tomb. Holds the silence of the place it grew. Items made of it are quieter than they should be — footfalls, drawn blades, voices near them.

materials.notes: Tier 3. Original. Not 'evil wood' — silence wood. Sound around a ghostwood object is dampened (tonal: gives the player a stat advantage on Sense-stealth at cost of being deeply unsettling in social use).

materials.name: Linen
materials.notes: Flax fiber. Common cloth; bandages, undergarments, sails.

materials.name: Wool
materials.notes: Sheep fiber. Cloaks, tunics, blankets. Holds warmth wet or dry.

materials.name: Cotton
materials.notes: Plant fiber. Lighter than linen, softer than wool. Mid-tier garments.

materials.name: Hemp
materials.notes: Coarse, durable. Rope, sailcloth, sacking.

materials.name: Silk
materials.notes: Tier 2-3. Luxurious; takes dye brilliantly. Required for some divinatory garments.

materials.name: Leather
materials.notes: Cured hide. Armor, bindings, belts, scabbards. Standard tanned cow/ox.

materials.name: Heavy Hide
materials.notes: Uncured or thick-cured large-beast hide (boar, aurochs, bear). Heavier armor stock.

materials.name: Parchment
materials.notes: Treated animal skin. Writing substrate; spell scribing in many traditions.

materials.name: Calf Vellum
materials.notes: Tier 2. Higher-grade parchment from young calf. Civic ledgers and high-cost scribing.

materials.name: Dragonscale (loose)

witness_payload.witness_summary: Loose scale from a dragon — typically shed, occasionally taken. Carries faint resonance of its parent's element. Crafts incorporating dragonscale risk attracting the dragon's attention if it lives.

materials.notes: Tier 4. SRD-attested. Original twist: if parent dragon still alive, items made carry an Echo back to it (Notice +2 with dragon faction at use).

materials.name: Salt (common)
materials.notes: Table salt. Preservation, scattering wards, mundane cooking. Distinct from Greywake's worked salts.

materials.name: Sulfur
materials.notes: Yellow brimstone. Alchemy, smoke-bombs, gunpowder analogues. Banned in some civic codes.

materials.name: Mercury (quicksilver)
materials.notes: Tier 2. Liquid metal. Mirror-silvering, alchemical solvent, scrying basin. Toxic; long-handlers lose Sense over time (handled by adapter, not material data).

materials.name: Phosphor Dust
materials.notes: Glows faintly in dark; ignites in air if loose. Light-glyphs, signal flares.

materials.name: Herb Bundle (mixed)
materials.notes: Generic apothecary bundle: rosemary, sage, wormwood, yarrow, etc. Regional substitutes documented in regional packs.

materials.name: Bone Meal
materials.notes: Ground bone — agricultural and necromantic both. Source provenance matters in some traditions (human/animal/unknown).

materials.name: Blood-Binder (dried)

witness_payload.witness_summary: Dried blood (usually animal) prepared for pact and binding work. Source must be declared at crafting; using human blood without declaration triggers contradiction.

materials.notes: Tier 2. Declared animal source is mundane; undeclared source is cursed. Universally banned in some civic codes; common in others.

materials.name: Ash (worked)
materials.notes: Pyre or hearth ash; sometimes named-pyre ash (provenance noted separately). Banishment circles, mourning rites.

materials.name: Iron-Gall Ink
materials.notes: Standard scribing ink. Civic ledgers, scribed scrolls, mundane records.

materials.name: Beeswax
materials.notes: Sealing wax, candles, waterproofing. Distinct from Greywake marrow-wax.

materials.name: Essential Oil (mixed)
materials.notes: Distilled botanical. Anointing, perfume, alchemical solvent.

materials.name: Crystal Dust

witness_payload.witness_summary: Ground quartz/calcite with weak resonant memory. Used in scrying focuses, alchemical amplifiers, abjuration powders.

materials.notes: Tier 2-3. Lower-grade carrier of metaphysical signal; pairs with stronger reagents.

materials.name: Pewter
materials.notes: Tin-lead-copper alloy. Tableware, tankards, mass-cast trinkets. Soft; deforms before breaking.

materials.name: Brass (baseline)
materials.notes: Copper-zinc alloy. Distinct from mat_brass_greywake (regional, foundry-hallmarked). Instruments, fittings, hinges.

materials.name: Watered Steel (Damascus)
materials.notes: Tier 2-3. Folded high-carbon steel with characteristic wavy pattern. Edge holds twice mundane steel; smiths swear by it. Historical attestation: Persian/Indian metallurgy.

materials.name: Mithral

witness_payload.witness_summary: Silver-bright alloy lighter than aluminum and harder than steel. Fey traditions claim it as 'truesilver' — does not tarnish, holds enchantment well, ignores some abjurations.

materials.notes: Tier 3-4. SRD-attested. Armor made of mithral counts as one category lighter for stealth/strength prerequisites.

materials.name: Adamantine

witness_payload.witness_summary: Black-gray alloy of nigh-unbreakable strength. Dwarven and dread-king metallurgy traditions both claim it. Items made of it cannot be sundered by mundane means; deal critical damage to objects.

materials.notes: Tier 4. SRD-attested. Heavy, hard to work, expensive.

materials.name: Sapphire
materials.notes: Tier 3. Blue corundum. Royal/judicial associations; some traditions use as truth-focus.

materials.name: Ruby
materials.notes: Tier 3. Red corundum. Most valuable corundum; folk-belief: heats blood, protects from poison.

materials.name: Emerald
materials.notes: Tier 3. Green beryl. Folk-belief: reveals lies, eyes of statues. Cracks under stress.

materials.name: Diamond
materials.notes: Tier 3-4. Hardest known stone; cuts glass, focuses light. Required component in some Restoration-tier spell traditions (consumed at cast).

materials.name: Moonstone

witness_payload.witness_summary: Adularescent feldspar that catches light like a tide. Folk and scholarly traditions agree: dreams settle on moonstone overnight. Holds a faint echo of the wearer's recent dreams.

materials.notes: Tier 2. One of the few baseline gemstones with light metaphysical signature. Folk: divination, fertility, safe sea passage.

materials.name: Onyx
materials.notes: Tier 2. Black banded chalcedony. Funerary and necromantic traditions both use it; signet rings and curse-mounting. SRD: spell component for Animate Dead.

materials.name: Malachite
materials.notes: Tier 1-2. Green banded copper carbonate. Carved decorative; folk-protective against evil eye (worn near children).

materials.name: Lapis Lazuli
materials.notes: Tier 2. Ultramarine pigment source; ground to make the most expensive blue paint in the world. Religious icons, illumination.

materials.name: Amber (baseline)
materials.notes: Tier 1-2. Fossilized tree resin. Inclusions (insects, debris) raise value. Distinct from mat_drowned_amber (Greywake regional).

materials.name: Pearl
materials.notes: Tier 2-3. Mollusk-secretion biomineral. Coastal traditions: sea-witness; oath-binding. SRD: spell component for some divinations.

materials.name: Cedar
materials.notes: Aromatic softwood. Moth-repellent; preferred for chests, scroll cases. Religious traditions: incense, temple beams.

materials.name: Willow
materials.notes: Flexible, waterside. Baskets, wattle, charcoal for ink. Folk: bark steeped for fever (salicin).

materials.name: Hazel
materials.notes: Coppice wood. Divining rods (water-witching), wands, wattle. Folk: hazel rods point at hidden water.

materials.name: Rowan
materials.notes: Folkloric anti-witch wood (Celtic/Norse). Threshold posts, walking staves, charm-rod cores. Reads as 'protective' across many traditions.

materials.name: Juniper
materials.notes: Aromatic. Berries flavor spirits; smoke for ritual purification (Greek, Slavic, North African traditions).

materials.name: Mahogany
materials.notes: Tier 2. Tropical hardwood. Furniture, fine cabinetry, ship rails. Imported from southern continents.

materials.name: Teak
materials.notes: Tier 2. Oily tropical hardwood. Ship decking; water-rot resistant. Burmese/SE Asian historical attestation.

materials.name: Hawthorn
materials.notes: Dense thorny. Cudgels, hedging, faerie-folklore boundary marker (a hawthorn alone in a field is not cut). Akin to blackthorn but with stronger threshold-significance.

materials.name: Rawhide
materials.notes: Uncured hide. Drumheads, dog chews, lashing. Hardens like wood when wet then dried.

materials.name: Sinew
materials.notes: Animal tendon, processed. Bowstring backing, fine lashing. SC-08 candidate (creature-derived but using material_fiber for now).

materials.name: Gut String
materials.notes: Processed gut (sheep/cat). Musical instrument strings, surgical thread, bowstrings. SC-08 candidate.

materials.name: Down Feathers
materials.notes: Soft underfeathers (goose, eider). Pillow stuffing, quilted gambeson padding, fletching down. SC-08 candidate.

materials.name: Fur (assorted)
materials.notes: Various trim-grade furs (rabbit, fox, beaver). Cold-weather lining. Source/quality matters for value. SC-08 candidate.

materials.name: Spider Silk (raw)

witness_payload.witness_summary: Strands harvested from large spider species. Stronger than steel by weight; takes dye unevenly. Some traditions: spiders weave fate; thread holds a fragment of that.

materials.notes: Tier 3. SRD-adjacent (giant spider silk). Used in light armor, ritual bindings, divinatory cordage.

materials.name: Canvas
materials.notes: Heavy hemp or linen weave. Sails, tents, painted panels, tarpaulins.

materials.name: Felted Wool
materials.notes: Wool processed by heat/moisture/pressure into dense matted fabric. Boot liners, gambeson layers, yurt walls.

materials.name: Dire-Beast Hide

witness_payload.witness_summary: Hide from a dire-class beast (dire wolf, dire bear, dire boar). Carries trace of the beast's pre-death intent — armor or trophy made from it occasionally provokes hostile animals.

materials.notes: Tier 2-3. SC-08 candidate. Source creature affects effect: dire bear hide grants intimidation in social use; dire wolf hide warmth + tracking aura.

materials.name: Reptile Scales
materials.notes: Crocodile/giant lizard/serpent scales. Scale armor stock. Tier 2. SC-08 candidate.

materials.name: Fish Scales (large)
materials.notes: Sturgeon, tarpon, large salmon. Iridescent decorative use; fish-leather backing. SC-08 candidate.

materials.name: Chitin (insectoid)
materials.notes: Tier 2. Plates harvested from large insectoid beasts. Hard, light, brittle when struck wrong. SC-08 candidate.

materials.name: Giant Arthropod Shell
materials.notes: Tier 2-3. Carapace from giant crabs, scorpions, etc. Shield stock. SC-08 candidate.

materials.name: Saltpeter
materials.notes: Potassium nitrate. Preservation, alchemical oxidizer, smoke-bomb component. Civic-regulated in many cities.

materials.name: Charcoal
materials.notes: Carbonized wood. Smithing fuel, sketching, water purification, ink base.

materials.name: Soot
materials.notes: Carbon-black residue. Pigment, ink base, disguise compound.

materials.name: Alchemical Acid (vial)
materials.notes: Etching, alchemical processing, splash weapon (1d6 acid damage in many rule frames).

materials.name: Lye
materials.notes: Caustic alkali. Soap-making, paper processing, corpse-rendering.

materials.name: Alum
materials.notes: Mordant for dyes, water clarifier, styptic for shaving cuts.

materials.name: Gum Arabic
materials.notes: Acacia resin. Binder for inks, paints, alchemical pastes.

materials.name: Frankincense
materials.notes: Tier 2. Aromatic resin. Religious incense across many traditions; folk-belief: drives off harmful spirits.

materials.name: Myrrh
materials.notes: Tier 2. Aromatic resin. Embalming, funerary incense, antiseptic. Companion-pairing with frankincense.

materials.name: Camphor
materials.notes: Crystalline aromatic. Embalming, moth-repellent, alchemical solvent. Folk: drives away the unburied.

materials.name: Mandrake Root

witness_payload.witness_summary: Human-shaped root. Powerful narcotic/hallucinogen; folk-belief screams when uprooted. Drowned Church variant: 'practiced mandrake' carries the screamer's witness — uses in dream-walking, oath-breaking, false-confession.

materials.notes: Tier 2-3. Civic-restricted in most cities. Source declaration matters.

materials.name: Wormwood (dried)
materials.notes: Bitter herb. Absinthe production, vermifuge, banishment circles, marginalia ink-bittering.

materials.name: Asafoetida
materials.notes: Pungent gum-resin. Indian/Persian historical attestation. Cooking spice; folk: wards against malign spirits (smell does the work).

materials.name: Valerian Root
materials.notes: Sedative herb. Sleep aid, anxiolytic in tinctures. Cats are drawn to it.

materials.name: Animal Blood (fresh)

witness_payload.witness_summary: Fresh animal blood. Cheaper and weaker than dried blood-binder; spoils in hours. Used in immediate-effect rites (apotropaic warding, fresh-blood scrying). Source declaration required.

materials.notes: Tier 1. SC-08 candidate. Distinct from mat_blood_binder (which is dried, durable). Useful for ritual immediacy, not for storage.

materials.name: Marrow (animal)

witness_payload.witness_summary: Bone marrow. Substrate for marrow-wax production (Greywake Drowned Church specialty). Carries the witness of the bone's origin.

materials.notes: SC-08 candidate. Pan-world substrate; Greywake's Drowned Church renders it heretically (see mat_marrow_wax_trace).

materials.name: Predator Bile
materials.notes: Tier 2. Bile from carnivore (wolf, big cat, raptor). Alchemical solvent, poison vector, leather processing. SC-08 candidate.

materials.name: Aberrant Ichor

witness_payload.witness_summary: Fluid harvested from aberration-class creatures (mind-things, deep-things, wrongly-made beasts). Resists declaration: even the harvester rarely knows what they took. Substrate for high-tier psionic-adjacent alchemy.

materials.notes: Tier 3-4. SC-08 candidate. Rare; contested by multiple traditions (Drowned Church wants it, civic authorities ban it).

materials.name: Tallow (rendered)
materials.notes: Rendered animal fat. Candles, soap, leather conditioning, food. SC-08 candidate (creature-derived but mundane processing).

materials.name: Predator Fangs
materials.notes: Wolf, big cat, large reptile. Carved into amulets, knife pommels, ritual implements. SC-08 candidate.

materials.name: Raptor Claws
materials.notes: Large bird-of-prey or wyvern-kin talons. Ritual implements, prestige hunting trophies. SC-08 candidate.

materials.name: Horn (ungulate)
materials.notes: Goat, cow, antelope, aurochs horn. Drinking vessels, signal horns, bow nocks, powder flasks. SC-08 candidate.

materials.name: Beast Sinew (large)
materials.notes: Tier 1-2. Heavy tendon from large beasts (bear, aurochs, megafauna). Composite bow backing, heavy bindings. SC-08 candidate. Distinct from mat_sinew (smaller animals).

materials.name: Raptor Feathers (flight)
materials.notes: Eagle, hawk, owl primary feathers. Fletching arrows; ritual headgear; quill pens. SC-08 candidate.

materials.name: Pitch
materials.notes: Tar from pine resin or coal. Sealing hulls, waterproofing roofs, torches, incendiary mixtures.

materials.name: Salt-Iron

witness_payload.witness_summary: Bog iron pulled from the salt-marshes north of Greywake. Smelts brittle but takes a wicked edge. Holds memory of the fountain's pressure — items forged of it 'remember the tide.' On a nat-1 attack roll, the weapon snaps along a salt vein.

materials.notes: Heretical reading of mundane bog iron + cold-iron folklore. Greywake-only because of the salt-marsh geography + the fountain's metaphysical pressure that the iron 'remembers.' Recipe sink: salt-iron dagger (slice recipe #1).

materials.name: Bell-Tin

witness_payload.witness_summary: Tin recovered from the salvage of old Bell Court bells that were retired or cracked. Carries faint resonance — tools of bell-tin ring softly when struck near civic spaces.

materials.notes: Civic-origin metal. Bell-Marked Charms made with bell-tin can be 'recognized' by Bell Court officials at attune-ceremony (mechanical: Notice +1 if charm used in a magistrate's presence). Recipe sink: Bell-Marked Charm (slice recipe #2).

materials.name: Drowned Bronze

witness_payload.witness_summary: Bronze retrieved from sunken civic and church wreckage in the shallows. Carries the witness of whatever the wreck once was — shield, bell-rim, altar lip. Crafts inherit a faint trace of the original purpose.

materials.notes: Origin matters — Drowned Church may claim items made from church-source drowned bronze (Faith Meter:Umberlee or Notice consequence at craft commit, decided by State Manager via witness binding roll). Recipe sink: Drowned Bronze Buckler (slice recipe #3).

materials.name: Greywake Brass

witness_payload.witness_summary: Brass cast in Greywake foundries from copper-tin-zinc mixes. Mundane-adjacent; carries only the faintest civic record (the foundry's hallmark). Used for non-mystical fittings, hinges, instrument casings, salt-battery casings.

materials.notes: The 'almost-mundane' Greywake metal. Useful because it carries the brass_greywake tinting WITHOUT the metaphysical weight of salt-iron or drowned bronze. Tinker-friendly for salt-battery casings.

materials.name: Salt (Greywake)

witness_payload.witness_summary: Reagent-grade salt harvested from the Greywake salt-pans. Distinct from common table salt in that the salt-pans sit downstream of the leaking fountain — the salt is 'practiced' even before any human touches it.

materials.notes: Greywake's working salt. Cheap, omnipresent, but never truly mundane in this region. Substrate of dozens of recipes. Recipe sink: Salt-Iron Dagger, Bell-Marked Charm, Drowned Bronze Buckler (slice recipes #1, #2, #3).

materials.name: Butcher's Salt

witness_payload.witness_summary: Salt blessed and cut by Marrow-Saint Ilyra's hands during specific Drowned Church rites. Carries the witness of the Marrow-Saint and the rite. Used in preservation of meat, of bodies, and of secrets.

materials.notes: Doctrinal Drowned Church material. Use without permission counts as taboo violation (drowned_church.json — taboo: unauthorized_butcher_salt_use). Recipe sink: Vial of Marrow-Wax Sealant (slice recipe #4).

materials.name: Fountain Water (raw)

witness_payload.witness_summary: Black seawater that leaks UPWARD from the dry fountain at the Market District's heart. Cannot be made still by mundane means — moves against gravity in containers, eats brass, blesses or curses depending on the witness of the drawer.

materials.notes: Center of Greywake's metaphysical pressure. Drawing it is itself an act some factions watch for. Notice +1 on any draw. Recipe sink: Vial of Practiced-Name Water (slice intermediate, feeds into Bell-Marked Charm).

materials.name: Practicing Water (intermediate)

witness_payload.witness_summary: Fountain water that has been spoken-over by a practitioner with a Bell-Marked Charm or Drowned Church standing. Now holds a 'practiced name' — a faint, repeatable witness signature that can be transferred into crafts.

materials.notes: Intermediate. Produced by R-08 doctrinal rite (substrate: practicing_word). Cannot be created without prerequisite charm or standing — gates downstream recipes. Recipe sink: Bell-Marked Charm (slice recipe #2).

materials.name: Marrow-Wax (trace)

witness_payload.witness_summary: Wax rendered from bone-marrow under Drowned Church sealing rite. Holds the witness of whatever (or whoever) the marrow came from. Used to seal documents, doors, mouths.

materials.notes: Source declaration matters: animal-marrow is permitted under Marrow-Saint Ilyra's standing rite (no penalty); human-marrow without declaration = cursed (contradiction event). NPC Ilyra holds the legitimate supply chain. Recipe sink: Vial of Marrow-Wax Sealant (slice recipe #4); Marrow-Wax Seal of Ilyra (canonical baseline character bound item).

materials.name: Unrecorded Ink (base)

witness_payload.witness_summary: Ink mixed with butcher's salt, fountain-water, and the ashes of a Bell Court ledger page that was officially burned for falsification. Writes lines that cannot be 'witnessed' by Bell Court instruments. Civic contraband.

materials.notes: Writes that resist being noticed by the civic record system. Possession alone is a Bell Court taboo violation if discovered. Counter-substrate is the Unrecord spell (Imposed, L3). Recipe sink: vial of Unrecorded Ink (slice recipe #5).

materials.name: Salt-Rime

witness_payload.witness_summary: Crystalline crust that forms overnight on metal and stone within sight of the fountain. Visually beautiful, mechanically inert until applied — when applied to a wound or to a brand, marks the bearer 'recognized but not yet named' (Greywake condition).

materials.notes: Atmospheric byproduct of the Greywake metaphysical climate. Common, cheap, but you cannot ship it — outside region_greywake it crumbles to common salt within hours.

materials.name: Drowned Amber

witness_payload.witness_summary: Tide-tumbled amber pulled from the shore north of the salt-pans. Inclusions are not insects — they are scraps of paper, fragments of bell-clappers, the occasional fingernail. Each piece holds a discrete 'frozen' witness from the time the wreck happened.

materials.notes: Tier 3. Greywake's prestige metaphysical material. Drowned Church will pay for any piece whose inclusion matches a missing-presumed-dead church record. Tide League speculates on it. Item-soul substrate (R-73 schema candidate).

materials.name: Salt-Pan Brine

witness_payload.witness_summary: Raw seawater concentrated in the Greywake salt-pans before crystallization. Higher canon-pressure than processed salt — the pans sit closer to the fountain than the salt-houses do.

materials.notes: Cheap, abundant, awkward to transport (liquid). Alchemy substrate; cannot be shipped outside region without crystallizing en route (becomes mat_salt_reagent within ~3 days).

materials.name: Salt-Pan Crust

witness_payload.witness_summary: Top crust scraped from a fully-evaporated salt-pan. Mineral-rich (trace iron, copper, fountain-residue). Used in stronger rite preparations than common salt-reagent.

materials.notes: Tier 1-2. More potent than mat_salt_reagent for some rites; rougher texture. Drowned Church surgeons sometimes prefer it for warding salt-circles.

materials.name: Marrow-Saint Thread

witness_payload.witness_summary: Sinew (animal, declared) cured under Marrow-Saint Ilyra's surgical rite. Used for suturing wounds that would otherwise scar irreversibly, and for binding heretical-surgery grafts. Heals what it sews; remembers what it healed.

materials.notes: Tier 2. Drowned Church exclusive supply chain (Ilyra). Unsanctioned use of thread (without rite or declared source) triggers Faith:Umberlee -1, Notice +1.

materials.name: Bone Needle (Drowned Church)

witness_payload.witness_summary: Needle carved from a Drowned Church reliquary bone-stock under Ilyra's rite. Surgical fineness; some say each needle 'remembers' the saint whose bone it came from.

materials.notes: Tier 2. Paired with mat_marrow_saint_thread for sanctioned surgical work. Source declaration mandatory (the church keeps a ledger).

materials.name: Reliquary Gauze

witness_payload.witness_summary: Linen woven and salt-cured to wrap reliquary objects (saints' bones, drowned-church seals). When applied to wounds, transfers a faint Faith:Umberlee witness to the wound bearer.

materials.notes: Tier 1-2. Available from Drowned Church infirmaries; gray-market grade exists (no rite, no witness). Practical and devotional uses overlap.

materials.name: Civic Seal Wax (Bell Court)

witness_payload.witness_summary: Bell-tin-shavings mixed into beeswax under a magistrate's hand. When stamped, the seal counts as Bell Court witness; tampering produces a visible discoloration (the wax 'tells').

materials.notes: Tier 2. Legitimate civic substrate (counter to mat_marrow_wax_trace, which is Drowned Church sealing). Use without authorization (forgery) is a Bell Court taboo.

materials.name: Bell-Certified Ink

witness_payload.witness_summary: Iron-gall ink fortified with bell-tin shavings and consecrated to Bell Court records. Writes that count as canonical civic record; resists Unrecord (DC +2 against attempts to scrub).

materials.notes: Tier 2. Direct counter-substrate to mat_unrecorded_ink_base. Two civic record substrates fighting; the slice's first economic conflict.

materials.name: Civic Paper (Bell-Watermarked)

witness_payload.witness_summary: Linen-rag paper watermarked with the Bell Court seal at manufacture. Used for civic contracts, debt records, magistrate orders. Counterfeiting requires either an inside hand or the destruction of a real sheet.

materials.notes: Tier 2. Substrate for civic contracts (couples with mat_bell_certified_ink). One sheet = one civic record-page.

materials.name: Scrip Paper (Tide League)

witness_payload.witness_summary: Lighter, rougher paper used for Tide League salt-scrip and trade memos. NOT civic-canonical (Bell Court does not accept it as record). Volatile substrate — scrip itself trades against fountain pressure.

materials.notes: Tier 1-2. Mechanically coupled with the salt-scrip volatility model (v0.4 Bundle A). Tide League prints scrip on this; speculators trade it.

materials.name: League Seal Brass

witness_payload.witness_summary: Brass cast at the Tide League's broker-house furnaces. Used for trade seals, contract pendants, broker badges. Identifies the bearer as League-affiliated; carries a witness of the broker who cast it.

materials.notes: Tier 2. Trade-faction marker. Civic authorities (Bell Court) treat League seals as legitimate trade record but NOT civic record.

materials.name: Heretical Choir Brass

witness_payload.witness_summary: Brass cast in undeclared furnaces — usually by heretical Drowned Church splinters who refuse civic foundry oversight. Items made of it ring oddly under church-sanctioned bells; sometimes the ring sustains after the bell falls silent.

materials.notes: Tier 3. Possession alone is a Bell Court taboo violation + Drowned Church orthodoxy violation simultaneously. Two-front contraband.

materials.name: Listening Child's Pebble

witness_payload.witness_summary: Beach pebbles the Listening Child collects and gives away. Each pebble has held the Child's attention for some unmeasured duration. Carries a fragment of whatever the Child was listening to when she picked it up.

materials.notes: Tier 1 by value, Tier 3 by metaphysical signature. Cannot be purchased — the Child only gives them. Refusal to accept is itself a canon-event in some workflows (X.14). One of canonical baseline character Khojen's bound items.
